title: Missing important things.
body:
Missing pride month, black history month, and more. These things are important you take them away we will still celebrate but you trying to hide problems is causing the problems.

These months are in remembrance of those who fought for people’s rights and to keep remembering that we are all people. 

As stated by Google “Black History Month was created to focus attention on the contributions of African Americans to the United States. It honors all Black people from all periods of U.S. history, from the enslaved people first brought over from Africa in the early 17th century to African Americans living in the United States today.” 

And then pride month, “Pride Month honors the Stonewall Uprising of 1969, which led to the modern gay rights movement. On June 28, 1969, New York City police raided the Stonewall Inn, a gay bar in Greenwich Village. The raid sparked six days of protests by LGBTQ people. The protests galvanized the gay rights movement.” 

So many of these events brought forth to show issues and to remember that we are all valid no matter race, sexuality, gender or anything. When people try to erase existence of others it just makes issue worse. Black history month created in remembrance of what had happened in the past and the slavery and how we’ve over come most of it but they’re still human and people. Pride month created after police brutality on a LGBTQ bar that cause violence to break out when provoking and hurting the public. 

Stop trying to erase the importance of acceptance.

title: Stop removing holidays
body:
There are several great alternatives to Google Calendar, depending on your needs:

Privacy-Focused Alternatives
	•	Proton Calendar – End-to-end encrypted, from the makers of ProtonMail.
	•	Tuta Calendar – Privacy-focused with encryption, part of the Tutanota ecosystem.

Feature-Rich & Productivity-Oriented
	•	Microsoft Outlook Calendar – Best for integration with Office 365.
	•	Zoho Calendar – Good for businesses, integrates with Zoho apps.
	•	Notion Calendar (formerly Cron) – Great for Notion users, minimalistic UI.

Open-Source & Self-Hosted
	•	Nextcloud Calendar – Self-hosted, integrates with Nextcloud.
	•	Etar Calendar – Open-source for Android, works with CalDAV.

Minimalist & Focused on Simplicity
	•	Apple Calendar – Simple, built-in for Apple users, syncs with iCloud.
	•	Fantastical – Mac/iOS only, excellent UI with natural language

title: I’m haunted by the Europeans.
body: Google Calendar is a very convenient tool to use when managing your day to day life, especially with another person. I do recommend it over the default calendar app, but the only dispute I have with it is that there’s a constant bug that sets your time zone to Greenwich Mean Time (GMT), which is located within the UK. I’ve seen that many other people online have dealt with a similar problem and have found no real solution besides changing it manually. Unless you live in this area, you run the risk of finding out last minute that you the app has switched the time of an appointment in your calendar without notifying you. As someone who has health issues and schedules doctor visits constantly, and often times in advance, it’s frustrating to catch these thing last minute and have to battle with the app for it to stay corrected. It seems this bug does not affect all users, as the other person in my calendar does not experience this and all settings within the app and my phone itself are set to the correct time zone. Unfortunately for me it simply becomes aggravating after a while. Google I pray you fix this bug for the sake of my sanity. Thank you.

title: ez pz
body:
before you read more reviews i just wanted to point out that almost 100% of the negative reviews are from user error. it's crazy that that amount of people don't understand how to set up events correctly (which could be blamed on a "hard to use" app but this is NOT the case). 

what i like:
- easy to navigate 
you can view your calendar a variety of ways and it's easy to select in and out of them
- easy to schedule
really easy to add events or tasks (and change their repetition)
- can sync with other outside calendars and other google apps (can sync apple calendar & can add events from gmail)
i made mine automatically grab events from my gmail and it added birthdays from my apple calendar directly onto the app
- can layer events from multiple emails
i have five gmails and it can have events from all of them at once in one place 
- functions great and has minimal issues/bugs
i havent dealt with a glitch nor bug yet PLUS theyre constantly updating the app to fix these nonexistent bugs
- free and can access offline

what i don't like:
- lack of colors to choose from
it comes with 12 colors but some of them are too similar. i wish i could create custom colors, too
- sharing calendar on mobile device specifically 
i had to fight in order to share my calendar with others WITHOUT them being able to edit it also. had to log into my pc and my phone and navigate it at the same time just to let someone see my calendar

overall, it's a great organizational tool to use for scheduling and planning. sets up fantastically and works extremely well. do yourself a favor and get this app!!

I love Google and Apple and usually have no problem getting them to work together. Google calendar apps on phone iPad are great and I have no complaints for either of those. 

My one major frustration is that the Google calendar app is not available for Apple watch and I have to make all my Google calendars sync to iCal, so my events can even show up on my watch. I would LOVE for Apple and Google to work together so Google Calendar could be a direct option for watch complications on the watch face.  It doesn’t ever seem to work perfectly because it needs the “middle man” of iCal to make it show up and something always is disconnecting between the two.

title: Great butttt could use improvements
body:

Sense losing reminders we’ve lost an extra way to keep track of things. Coming from someone who heavily relies on Google Calendars for their sanity, this was kind of a big loss. I previously used tasks to track my bills so they could be checked off once paid while also be reoccurring. But now all my tasks/reminders are the same color as I have to use tasks for reminders. 

It’s definitely not the end of the world but it would be more useful if we could also color code our individual tasks or color code the different task lists. Another potential option that could be beneficial is to allow for a reoccurring events to have a completed option as long as it would still show on its next reoccurrence as “not completed.”

title: App Issues, please fix!!
body:

title: Three suggestions and one problem
body:
I am a mother and I primarily use calendar with the tasks feature to block time for my recurring household tasks (such as cleaning, cooking, exercising) along with managing appointments, events, and work.

I was a loyal Timeful user before Google bought it out. Timeful’s unique integration of organizing my checklist into an hourly timeline helped keep me accountable and realistic in my time management, and I’ve been waiting (im)patiently😅 in anticipation of Google bringing it back. In some ways Google has improved on Timeful, but a few of the best features are missing and I’d love to see them come back.

  1. The tasks listed in the hourly view used to have a little empty circle on the left side of the bar. After completing a task I could simply tap the circle and a check mark would appear in the circle and a line would go through the writing. Basically, it was way easier and more satisfying to mark a task completed. 
  2. I could assign a duration to a task and the proper amount of time would be blocked off on the calendar. Let’s say I want to run on the treadmill for an hour, and it takes me ten minutes to do the dishes. I could allocate different lengths of time to each task and piece it into my hourly view to get a visual of the day. Right now all tasks default to 15 min. 
  3. Timeful used to keep a bank of my recurring tasks available to chose from daily. I created the list and I could easily drag and drop the tasks I chose from the list directly into my hourly view for the next day. It was a nice feature to use at bedtime to quickly plan my next day. 

There is also one problem with the current calendar. When I open a task to click “Mark completed”, a banner pops up at the bottom of the screen asking if I want to undo the action. If I’m trying to quickly mark several tasks completed, the banner blocks the “Mark completed” option on the next task and I have to wait until it goes away to mark the next task complete. It is frustrating and a waste of time. Please move the banner so I can quickly mark several tasks completed. Or better yet, see suggestion #1 above. 🤞😊

I love the option to color code events so I can quickly differentiate between school, work, church, family events, and doctor appointments. I also like that unmarked tasks follow you to the next day. It’s not perfect yet, but it’s the best calendar I’ve found since Timeful!!

I have missed meetings at times when I have not opened up the calendar app between accepting the invite and the time of the meeting. The only way I can guarantee that I’ll get the notifications is if I add the google account to the standard iPhone calendar, which will actually fetch the data from my google account and provide me notifications. I have messed with all notification settings, fetch/push days settings, background app refresh, etc. 2 stars because while everything else about the app is fine, this is an extraordinarily basic function. title: What's the point?
body:
New Review 
I came to Google because I loved having Reminders, Tasks and Google Keep Reminders all together in my calendar.  It WAS a good thing. But for Google it seems, if it’s good then it needs to be wrecked. And that’s exactly what Google has done.

📌Eliminated Reminders
📌Everything is now a task
📌Disconnected Google Keep Reminders from the calendar 
📌Google Task App is crappy, not showing half the tasks that I have on the calendar app, Tasks App doesn’t play well with Calendar App.

Seriously thinking about my options outside of Google now. So tired of Google “fixing” what’s not broken!😡

Old Review
So in Inbox for Google I set a reminder about a certain email. The reminder shows up in Google calendar but no indication of what email it's attached to. I click "see in email". It will not take me to Inbox, so I downloaded the regular email app (which is stupid...why should I have to duplicate?). The "link" takes me to the Google Mail app and that is where it ends. It doesn't link to the email, then I have to go open Inbox to locate the email in my pinned items. I would expect if the reminder is going to say view in email, then it is going to link direct to the email it is for, instead of leaving you scratching your head wondering what email it was. And what's the point of making you go to the email app that doesn't have the reminder attached to the email when you are going to have to go to the Inbox app anyway? It should take you direct to the email in question. IQTELL has this ability, it doesn't seem like Google should have a problem with that. It seems half baked to me. Dumb. If the reminder isn't going to take me directly to the email then I wish it would not clutter up my calendar.

title: Plain but good
body:
I am very old school, I generally use one of the classic hardback, spiral bound dayplanners, so I figured it was time for an update! I looked all over the app store for an app that would work for me, I probably downloaded over 20+ apps looking for a good fit, bc I like to see my entire month at a glance, just like I can with my dayplanner.

Most of the ones I found had every feature other than that, and the ones that did have it, you had to pay for the premium version of it in order to have that view.

Then my friend told me about google calendar, so I downloaded it and gave it a shot. It's not fancy, it doesn't come with all the bells and whistles, and pretty designs that the other apps do, but I don't need all that. 

It lets you view 6 weeks at a time, starting at the beginning of the current month. They have 12 different colors that you are able to color code your stuff with, although some colors are very similar, such as "blueberry" and "lavender," however, they have the full spectrum of the rainbow on there. It's mostly soft, muted colors, but there's obviously a huge difference in red, yellow, blue, etc.

I give it 4 stars instead of 5, bc the app icon always stays on the 31. I wish there was a way to have it accurately reflect the current date and time. You have to go into the actual app to see what day it is. Maybe a widget for the app?

Also, I wish there was a way to show the current 6 weeks, instead of previous weeks. For example, today is Wednesday, February 22, 2023. I wish it would show this week, starting Sunday, February 19, 2023, and then going to the last week of March, 2023, instead of starting at the beginning of February and going to the second week of March. 

However, beggars can't be choosers, and for a 100% complete free app, I'd say it's pretty dang good!

Old appointments can’t be seen or searched in the app, so it’s really only useful for day-to-day scheduling. Obviously Google cares more about Android, so this isn’t surprising - but it’s painful for anybody using iPhone/iPad.

title: Extremely disappointed they’re getting rid of Goals.
body:
Goals was perfect for developing habits. 
I used it for my workouts and loved how it would sync up with my Health app. 

The fact that you could easily reschedule missed events to later days was really helpful considering how seamless the process was. 

It made tracking events easy and the fact that the calendar would automatically move the goals around prior posted events was perfect. 

Really really disappointed in Google for this decision. I know I am not the only one who is confused as to why they would remove such a useful function. 

Recurring events by contrast is much clunkier by design and simply less practical for those with complex calendar events. It’s too bad because I would have even paid for Google Goals but no, they just decided to get rid of it entirely. Typical Google.

body:

But one thing that has really been frustrating me lately that would be SO easy to fix is the color options for events. I love colors and live a colorful life! 
When you go to Settings to the default color options for categories like Events and Reminders, it shows so many colors! But then if you want to change the color of event while creating/editing it, you have the much smaller, regular pool of colors to choose from. 
And on the computer, under the same place in Settings, there’s even a color gradient for you to pick/create your own color!!! But there is still the small option pool when changing the event color in creating/editing. 

I feel like this small change would SO GREATLY ENHANCE my experience on this app. As a full time working student with a busy schedule, I need a different color for each class/job/activity but I often have to repeat and it would just be awesome if I had more options! 
Thanks!

title: Not working well on iOS 15
body:
I’ve deleted the app after too many appointments disappearing. (I also had deleted the native calendar app due to missing appointments.)

For one of the latest disappearances, I received an email saying I deleted a meeting that I organized, which I didn’t. Participants emails which I didn’t add were listed in the email describing the calendar event. I was still able to join the meeting thanks to a separate email. Is it a security breach? A healthcare appointment also disappeared and one that was recurring that had Zoom information, gone. The only appointments that are consistently stable are ones created with third party apps.

Another problem that is exclusively Google is that there is no longer a way to manage my multiple calendars on my phone without having duplicate events appearing when my desktop calendars show the other calendars. I’ve reduced having 4 repetitions by not showing all calendars on 2 accounts on my desktop, but on the phone I still have to deactivate accounts from the calendar. The ability to have all 4 accounts active and hide events from repeating has been taken away! I have to forego managing my personal account calendar on my phone, the events of which I can only manage from one of my work emails. (I run 2 businesses and have a job!) And now I can’t add personal appointments from my phone. 

There must be a workaround but since events have been disappearing, I’m going back to pencil and paper.

—previous review—
Years ago I tried Calendar only to be frustrated. But now that I have 4 different Google calendars for 4 different purposes, this app has helped keep all appointments. Other apps have shown a repetition of events because each Google calendar on my desktop shows all 4 calendars. But this app enables viewing of only one entry each. Also, the graphics are not as distracting as they used to be, something that I had complained about previously. Google listened and improved the app. Who can ask for anything more?

body: The motto of this app is “Get Organized” and yet it’s missing some of the most simple features to be able to do precisely that. Despite the billions Google makes selling our private data they can’t (or won’t) design a decent calendar app. There is a bunch of basic functionality from the web version that is not available in the app. Basic enough to render the app useless. 1) The calendar colors available in the app do not match the colors available on the web version. Come on, this is too simple to believe. 2) The app will not dim past events even if that setting is turned on on the web version. Again, let’s get on the ball Google. 3) There is no ability to change the calendar that an event is scheduled under. I literally couldn’t believe this one. Scheduled a meeting with a professor under your personal calendar? Don’t expect to be able to change that in the app. The absence of this capability is stupefying. If you’re like me and you use your iPad Pro in place of a laptop when you leave home then you have to go onto the web and deal with the hassle of trying to get your browser to load google calendar in the browser window instead of redirecting you to the app. Why are you redirecting me to the very thing that isn’t working in the first place?! Why bother having the app?! 4) The default calendars under each of my accounts retain the name “Events” even when I change their names using the web version. Very frustrating when you have other calendars you’ve created called “Events” because you want your default calendar to be for every day things and consider “events” to be less frequent, bigger deals. Whatever the rationale a person has, they should be able to name the calendars whatever they want and have that reflected in the app. In sum, these issues are fundamental enough to render the app more of a frustration than an assistance. In the app I can view all of my accounts in one place, at least it has that going for it. Instead of spending who knows how much money designing the “Goals” section, how about Google fixes the basics. If it weren’t for the fact that my work requires the use of Google calendar I’d be off it in a heartbeat; which is really unfortunate, because the web version allows for so much more functionality than competitors.

On almost every app and website that exists nowadays, there’s an option to “share” some type of content, whether it be a page, news story, image, event, etc. Yet, somehow, the Google Calendar app has apparently forgotten to include such an option for calendar events!?

Wouldn't having the ability to share calendar events with someone via email or text message be a particularly valuable feature to offer? I don’t understand why that isn’t an available option yet. 

Specifically, my use case is that I create an event on my gmail account via my phone. Then I want to forward that event to another email of mine that has a different calendar associated with it. I don’t want those two calendars to be linked (one is personal, one for work), so I merely want to send a carbon copy of the event title, time, details, etc. to my work email, which I can then store as a new event on that calendar.

title: Bring back notifications for individual events
body: A few years ago when I first started using this app, you were able schedule notifications to go off a desired length of time before specific, individual events and reminders.  Now they have done away with this option, and it has decreased the usefulness and helpfulness of the calendar altogether.  Speaking as someone with ADHD who is also a visual learner, I use this calendar and the different color options to help me prioritize and keep track of things and not forget important commitments, such as doctors appointments and when bills are due.  But because of my ADHD brain, I need that extra help that sound notifications provide when it comes to one-time events that are outside my typical schedule, and unfortunately the developers got rid of the settings that used to allow you to do this.  I have looked everywhere on the app and on desktop, and the setting for this that used to be there is now nowhere to be found.  PLEASE BRING BACK THE OPTION TO SET SOUND NOTIFICATIONS FOR SINGLE EVENTS AND REMINDERS!!  If this setting doesn’t return I may be forced to use a different app/platform that does allow this option.

title: Fabulous Calendar Feature! ... For Free!
body:
I don’t know why I thought that the calendar feature on my IPhone would be too difficult for me to figure out how to use. However, after only a couple of “lessons,” (from the most knowledgeable, excellent IPhone expert I’ve ever known, my son, who’s currently at NCSU completing his degree in Computer Engineering 😉😂) I had gotten up to speed regarding the use of this great calendar feature! Like most people, no matter where I am on the go, I’ve got my cell phone with me. Now, this means that I’ve got my calendar with me, too... so no more making plans/appointments on a little paper calendar that you can fit it in your purse,  back pocket, random piece of paper, and then having to write what you scheduled down again several times on your calendar at home, at work, and wherever else you keep a calendar... or I remember the most frustrating thing for me!!  ... no more making an appointment for something like a follow up time to see your doctor or planning a lunch date, only to arrive home, check your calendar, and discover that you’d just double booked yourself... Once you were finished sweeping the floor, having gotten up most of your hair that you’d just torn out, and answered four IPhone calls, calmly explaining that the screaming that they’d just heard must have come from her TV and that she’d get that turned down right away...so sorry to have bothered you... yes, you never really do know these days... thank you for your concern... oh, yes. I definitely would do the same for you for sure...yada, yada, yada, yada, blah, blah... blllaaahhh. ...And then I 
 got myself calm and collected and decided which of the two that I’d double  booked was going to be the most gracious to me about my need to change the plans we’d just made.
Yep! I love the IPhone calendar!

title: 4.6 Is undeserved
body:
1) The UI lags too much.
2) Goals that I put in to fulfill everyday do not appear every day, not even in the same week.
3) It was designed by incompetent idiots, because if it were actually good, when I say “Mornings” are the best time for a certain goal, I reallllllly mean MORNINGS, not afternoons, and not whenever else the app randomly wants to put it.
4) I have to move a misplaced event more than once.
5) The UI is slow. If I am opting for the most simple pattern of events and goals, which would be to have the same things at the same time every single day, CLEARLY, it should be easy for the app to put everything in at the same time I put in as for the day before. It often either takes more than an hour to do it, or it doesn’t do it at all.
6) The design, the setup, the mobility is beautiful to me. But I want to throw my phone out the window when pretty design won’t do crap. 

I honestly don’t know how this app has 4.6 stars when many of the most recent reviews put it at sub-par quality. Looking pretty isn’t enough Google.

title: Readability Issues When Using Custom Calendar Colors with Dark Mode
body:
On the mobile app, when using dark mode, dark custom colors do not automatically make the text white. The result of this bug is unreadable content on the calendar (dark background with black text). 

I imagine this is due to the Google Calendar app using the default color values for iOS’s dark mode, black/grey for dark mode, white for light mode. 

This bug can be reproduced by setting a calendar to a dark custom color (HEX #00274C) in the web app, and then turning on dark mode in the iOS device settings.

title: V E R Y  G O O D. J U S T  O N E  S U G G E S T I ON
body:
I recently started distance learning because of COVID-19 and I had no clue how I was gonna manage my time and schedule. Usually we get teacher guidance but since we can’t see are teachers in person, they couldn’t rly give it to us. 

Anyways, I was browsing the App Store like usual when I came across this app. I downloaded it instantly and fell in love with it. It was exactly what I was looking for. I can add reminders to log on to a zoom, I can add due dates for assignments, and if I give it access to contacts, it can even add birthdays of my friends and family. 

Now it may sound like other calendar apps, but the thing that sets it apart are the amazing graphics. I get bored easily, but this app didn’t bore me. You can color code reminders and events which is amazing and each months have cute graphics and drawings. So yeah, it’s awesome.  

I just have one suggestion:
In the beginning, it was hard to navigate and understand how to add events and things like that. If possible, could you add a tutorial feature for people who are just starting out? I feel like that would be very helpful, and many would agree. 

Thanks for your time, and keep making great apps google :)

title: No Apple Watch/Subscribed Calendars
body:
Overall, it looks good but it’s missing the most important thing to be usable for me. I must have it in my Apple Watch and have a complication so I see the next event just by raising my wrist. Google, add this and you’ll win me over from Apple’s calendar.

The other issue is with subscribed calendars. Google’s platform is far superior to Apple because I can subscribe to an external calendar on the site and see it on my phone as well. Perfect, almost. I set up a subscription to my work calendar. We are fully hosted on Microsoft 365. I’m able to see everything that was created PRIOR to setting up the subscription however, nothing new is coming in. After an exhaustive search, this is a Google problem that has existed for a long time. Google, you need to give us an option for subscribed calendars to specify update frequency. A global setting is simply not sufficient. I have another subscribed calendar which only needs an update once per week but my work calendar needs updates every 15 minutes. 

I do know I can add my M366 calendar in the default Apple calendar and it works as expected. That’s not what I want. I want all of my calendars in one place.

title: I only use it about half the time
body:
The app is great to remind me of everything I entered into my calendar... from my desktop. 

But using the app itself to enter new appointments is ridiculously user UN-friendly. It’s cumbersome with lots of extra steps; it’s neither user-friendly nor is it intuitive. Half the time I realized that I’ve entered something incorrectly because of the extra steps. Overall, it’s pretty useless.

You’d think (especially in a world of touch screens) that one could easily just tap the day of the month to which you want to add an appointment... similarly to how one just clicks on the day of the month from the desktop... and immediately you’d find yourself entering an appointment for that day. Not so... The app has added a few steps for it’s users. When I’m in a hurry and someone wants to quickly set an appointment, I dread pulling up my Google calendar app.

In fairness to Google, I haven’t found a good calendar app yet on the market. But... it’s Google... come on, Google, you can do better.

title: Awesome App!
body:
After losing my entire Outlook Calendar during a PC switch, I started using the Google calendar, and I’ve never considered using anything else.

title: Impossible to read on mobile phone
body:
My wife and I started using Google calendar as iOS calendar does not allow us to share calendar events and it is working great. 

BUT iOS calendar has a HUGE advantage over Google Calendar, in that, it can be easily readable in week and month views. As we are 50+ years old we need a easily viewable calendar. I have searched the internet and the only suggestions are to turn on the maginifier or in crease the font size for the entire phone iOS. Not every app not iOS screens need to have gigantic font sizing just to be able to read google calendar. 

I develop websites and I always make sure the site scales to a reader on any device. So I know Google has enough resources and expert UI & UX developers to make this happen. 

As one posted on a website I found researching “Wait until you turn 40 plus and your vision needs assistance”

Please make Google Calendar MOBILE FRIENDLY”! I know Google AI demotes all websites in the searches if NOT MOBILE FRIENDLY. 

SO WE ARE DEMOTING THIS REVIEW FOR NOT BEING “MOBILE OR OLDER EYES FRIENDLY”

I like the Google calendar because I can print out my calendar from my desktop which I could not do using my iCloud calendar...maybe because my PC uses the Windows....so it’s a trade off. title: Great App-but the Goal settings need some adjustments
body:
I use this app so much and appreciate the personalization which I think is better than any other calendar app. I also love the option of setting goals, but have been very frustrated a few times with some of its functions and thought I could give a few suggestions that would make my experience and hopefully others more enjoyable.

1) The most frustrating aspect regarding goals by a long shot is the lack of an "undo" for when I accidentally set an event for the wrong day or time.  For example, I wrote an event for 2 days instead of one, went to change it right away, but after changing it back all my goals for that 2nd day were either moved to a different day or deleted. I find this very frustrating and since I assume I'm not the only person who accidentally puts the wrong time or day in sometimes, it would be nice if there was a way to combat it. It's also upsetting because it makes it look like I didn't finish many of my goals a certain week even though I did. Some solutions could be giving the choice of inputting goals certain days along with the calendar choosing times within your schedule (which I really appreciate), having an "Earlier" option, as well as a later, or (most ideally) having the system  be able to notice when events have been deleted and re-input goals that were temporarily deleted would all be helpful options. Even waiting until a new event is in for at least 10 seconds before changing the goals would save a lot of grief.

2) Just like it's nice to write notes on certain events, it'd be nice to write them for goals as well, such as writing what you want to cook for your cooking goal or what workout you want to do for your exercise goal that day. 

3) Lastly, when choosing the frequency of goals, certain options aren't available, like 5 or 6 times a month. If the user could just input "___ times  a (day/week/month)" that might be easier.

Thanks for your time, I really love this app and would love it even more if some of these changes could be made!

- The Google Home Mini doesn’t even read all the calendar events, so making the switch feels like a waste of time.
- In order to add a birthday under the actual “Birthdays” label — which would be beneficial both for uniformity, but also so that it’s shared on the family calendar, yet distinct — you have to have the birthday person in your contacts. My 10-month-old is not in my contacts. 
- The app lags TERRIBLY.
- What I put into the app doesn’t always sync to the computer. This includes when I tried to sync my iOS calendar. It showed up on the app, but not the computer, which is why I had to tediously add a year of birthdays and anniversaries and events.
- This one may seem small, but having switched from a calendar that offers this feature I can say it is incredibly convenient: The app icon doesn’t show the current date, only an image of “31”. 
- The calendar just feels sort of... cluttered. One thing I appreciated about the iOS calendar was its simplicity. If I could have the simplicity of the iOS calendar with the bright colors and view options of the Google Calendar, with the changes I mentioned, I think it would be perfect (for me).

I’m still exploring both the phone app and the computer, and I hope to post a more positive review soon. As of now, I’m really disappointed.

title: Additional feature request
body:
This is more of a request than a review, disclaimer. 

This app covers all the basics, but there are a few features that would end my quest for the perfect calendar once and for all. 

First, I need to be able to create an event template with preset alarms, times and notes. I know about recurring events but that only works when the recurrence is somewhat consisent. It does not work for people who pick up different shifts every week or visit grandma for the same 4 hours, same place, but on different days.  Honestly whyyyy does this not exist yet.

Second, I need to be able to organize my events into separate calendars but export them and share as a single calendar.  For a simple example, I have a work and personal calendar. If I share it with coworkers for scheduling, I don’t want them to see two calendars.  I want to share one consolidated calendar with the option to hide event details. Furthermore, if I want to see the schedules for 5 people to decide when to meet up for a band practice (for example), I dont want to see 6 calendars for each person. I either want one per person or one big calendar for all of them that I can easily turn off with one click.  Again, why isn’t this a thing? 

Third, I would like to be able to integrate other clock apps with this app to have more ringer options and a better interface for turning off reminders.  I want to be able to customize the message that appears when the alarm comes up for an upcoming event (ex: “Leave for work now or youre going to be late. Again. Xoxo”), customize the ringer sound and have a big button like the snooze button to turn off the event alarm. Swiping is not intuitive to me because there are two directions to swipe with different options - its too complicated. 

I wanted to write this as a review to give these ideas exposure in hopes that someone will pick them up and make a better app! Thank you!

title: Busy Family Sanity Saver - Mobile app needs to match web function
body:
I've been using Google calendar for years...YEARS. It's awesome. We have about 20 different calendars to keep up with between our family, work, activities, etc. I'd love to give this app 5 stars but there is a couple of things that need to be added:

* Desktop calendar you can choose which days to repeat. I.e. Weekdays (Monday - Friday), specific days. You can not easily do this from the repeat option in the app. Only all or none. You have to log into the desktop version to edit or create repeated events.

* Desktop computer you can easily update which calendar the event was created on if there was a mistake of adding an event to the originally created event. In the app, you're only able to edit the "default color."  You have to log into the desktop version to edit the original event and then are able to change the calendar to add the event.

* There is a workaround to share the colors, giving full rights to edit, delete, etc every event. But it would be nice to be able to add "Family Share" like most of the apps on the market to share every imported calendar, added calendars, etc. It would be great to be able to add any calendar, event (in the color required) automatically import into EVERYONE that needs to have the specific calendar. Having to log in to everyone's account to import from URLs, change colors, etc is tedious and time-consuming. However, this is vital to making sure everyone in our family knows where we're supposed to be.

title: Disappointing new “feature”
body:
We are big fans of Google products, but I recently discovered that Google Calendar is deleting anything that is more than 3 years old. Big Deal, you say, so what? Why do you need old stuff? 

We have health issues, some minor and some very major, Big League important. Google used to have a product called Google Health that was used to compile a history of your illnesses, surgeries, treatments, prescriptions, etc. They apparently couldn’t find a way to monetize it, so, Poof, it went away, and they sloughed everybody off to join Microsoft Health Vault. It, too, has gone away. 

Google Calendar is where we turned next to keep track of our appointments, decisions, and by using the Notes portion of the Event, we can add questions to be asked of our doctors and record their answers, when to refill medicines. By keeping track of ALL of our health visits, we had documentation for our tax filings. 

So, if you need something only for Tomorrow, use Google Calendar. If you want to review past events, then Calendar is not the tool you need.

title: MarkO
body: I have tried several calendars and have concluded that the Google calendar is my favorite. It offers great flexibility. I create a title for the event and select the time frame. Google lets me select multiple advance notifications, including a customized one. I can event pick from several colors to personally code my events with colors significant to me (e.g., urgent, family, shopping, medical, routine, entertainment, etc.). One of the coolest features is setting the location. Often when I start typing in an address or name of a place, the entire address appears and I just have to click on it. Then - thanks to Google maps - after I select the address, an image of the location appears after I save the address and the event. And I’m pretty sure that if you touch the address, it will take you to Google maps and give you directions to the location. Amazing! You can also post reminders on your calendar. A reminder will keep reappearing until you note that the task was completed. As with other calendars, there are multiple views. The calendar is user friendly, very functional and - excuse me, I can’t think of the technical term - easy on the eyes. I’ve never had a problem with it and have no criticism of it. It totally meets my needs and has exceeded my expectations. I do not normally do reviews, but actually felt obligated to do so when prompted by the pop up request. Great job, Google!

title: Good but needs work
body:
This app is good in several ways. I really like how it connects to my Google Calendar and sends me reminders, etc.
Aside from the glitches like freezing or losing an event I’m in the middle of creating that occasionally occur (& can be highly annoying especially when you’ve put in a ton of detailed info like ticket numbers, guests, etc.), the top 3 things I really wish they would fix are (in order of priority):
(1) Searches- When I do a search for a keyword, it only searches through future events. I frequently need to know the date a previous activity occurred, but I can’t do that through this app. Also it’s really picky about the keyword. For instance if I do a search for “pet,” but I’ve always written “pets,” it frequently won’t find the events.
(2) I can’t change which calendar an event is connected to after creating it. For instance I have a general Events calendar for myself, and I have a Traveling calendar that I share with other people. When you create an event and then go on to create a 2nd event, that 2nd event automatically connects to whichever calendar you were using for the previous event. I really don’t need people in my Traveling group to know when my OB-GYN appointment is or where my husband and I are going for date night. And there have been several times when I’m rushing to try to get the connection changed and have to get to a computer to fix it because the calendar is so tiny on a web browser on my phone.
(3) The photo for the location often has little to do with the actual location- it can be any random photo someone has uploaded, which is very unhelpful when I’m trying to identify something to do with the actual business and instead I’m seeing a picture of someone who once went to that business.

title: Best Free Calendar App You Can Get
body: I’ve tried all kinds of available calendar apps, but this one is by far my favorite! I often tell my friends to drop their apps and opt for Google Calendar because I really think it is so much better than any other free-cal app out there. I am easily able to look at my daily, weekly and monthly schedule- and I LOVE that the monthly outlook actually tells me what I have going on each day. I can also color-code events/calendars so I can see what realms I have working each day, AND it syncs up online so that I can use it on my computer too. I also have calendars made for my team so that I can put events in all of our schedules at one time. And I can set GOALS and make REMINDERS and CHECK THEM OFF AS I GO??? Amazing. I probably sound like a fake review right now, but I swear I am a human (who never even writes reviews) and I just really really love this app.  Do yourself a favor and get this.

I can’t even color code the events on her Android tablet although it lets me on my iPhone. It would be much more simple to see whose week it if each parent had their own color events. Also, a new calendar can’t be created for her parents and I to interact with the calendar from our own accounts. We will each have to use her login. And events can’t be categorized. My next disappointment is that each time the app is opened it is on the “Today” view not remembering that I last selected the “Month” view. The biggest let down is upon opening the app each date has to be selected for the events for that day to be loaded. I can understand this needing to be done once since they are being inputted from a different device, but each time the app is opened?! That’s just ridiculous! I am sadly surprised that Google has such a horrible app, especially for such a common type of app as a calendar.

Who puts the number in the middle?!?! It goes in the corner. Basically it looks awful! And in the schedule view they flipped the day of the week and the date and made them less bold and smaller. title: Excellent Calendar, even better with a few tweaks
body:
My school uses Google Suite for student email, handout distribution and storage, and turning in assignments, to name a few uses. I use Google Calendar to coordinate all of these things and record my homework. I have a color-coded calendar for each class so I can glance at my week and see my work load easily. Unfortunately, I have to set up each assignment as an event because reminders can’t attach to calendars or change their color. This makes it difficult to see a list of all my homework together, whereas with reminders, I could mark them as done and display them together.

I also encountered an issue where trying to share an event with someone while creating it would cause the event to not be created, but sharing the event after creating it would be successful. Still, these are minor problems and improvements and overall, this is one of the best calendar apps I’ve seen.

title: Extremely few features, Very Simple
body:
Beautiful, aesthetically pleasing, unsophisticated app. 

If you have simple, unsophisticated calendar needs, like tracking birthdays, doctor appointments, kid events, simple work schedule, and other such everyday events. Then this maybe the calendar app for you. 

Anything more sophisticated and this calendar app becomes extremely disappointing with very few features and make it difficult to update events and appointments. 

Even for reminders this app does not suite my needs. For reminders I will often add a client phone number or dial in number for the conversation, plus what the call is about. 

There is absolutely no way to add this info w/o it being “part” of the reminder memo itself. Meaning all info shows up in the subject line of “Call [Name] [phone #] [full memo]” - this would take up the whole calendar entry. Then suddenly the calendar entries are not so aesthetically pleasing anymore, they’re just crowded and long. 

CalenGoo is still the best as far as Google Calendar Apps go and best kept secret.

title: I like it, but it needs improvement
body:
This app is one of the most comprehensive as far as what I can do, but it needs fixing in a few areas. First of all, Goals are super glitchy and need improvement. I find that it’s super inconvenient that there is no option to select Goal time/date manually, you have to let the app decide for you. You can change manually it AFTER it is auto assigned, but you have to do them each individually. So if I have a 5 day workout goal and I want them all to be at specific times, I have to manually fix every single day and time to where I want it. It’s super inconvenient. It should simply be an option and nothing more to have the app select times and dates for your goals. Additionally, I find that sometimes they delete themselves, and also, if you set a goal it only lasts about three weeks before you have to recreate them again. You should be able to have the option to select the cut off date or have them running indefinitely, like you can with “Events.” It’s almost better to set your Goals as Events because Events actually works. 
Additionally, I find that when I swipe other to the next week it will sometimes ship months or years ahead for seemingly no reason.

title: Missing Desktop Functionality
body:
Hey google- 

Workflow issue here. I should be able to do everything on the app that I can do on the PC. This ONE feature has caused me to lower my rating from 5 to 2 stars, so I’d appreciate it if you’d fix it. 

ON PC I can select an event and change it from one calendar to another. On mobile, I have to copy it to the new calendar and then delete it from the old calendar to avoid duplicate events.

This wouldn’t be so bad if it was once in a while, but it happens every time an app or email adds something to my calendar on iphone because iphone inputs a default calendar. As someone who has to put a massive amount of events into a calendar from a mobile device, this will cause HOURS of extra work.

 Please add a feature to change an event’s calendar, even if it’s a roundabout way such as a single button that simultaneously duplicates the event to the selected calendar and deletes the old event. OR a confirmation dialog after “copy to...” that says, “Delete original event? [Yes] [No]” box.

Heck, add a, “Are you sure you want to delete this event? [Yes] [No]” box with a “[] Remember my choice for next time.” feature.

OTHERWISE: Great calendar. Really useful. Exactly what I need. If this is changed, my review will change to 5 stars and be updated accordingly.

title: Not enough notifications - stick with iCloud
body:
I switched to Google Calendar from iCloud for shared calendars with my family, only to realize a couple very unfortunate things:

1) There are no push notifications when a family member adds or updates an event on a shared calendar. iCloud would immediately notify in this case, saying <person> added an event to <calendar> or such. In Google Calendar, you need to be invited to each individual event (by email) to receive a notification (email, not push) when it is added. Further, there is no way to assign a default guest list for new events in a given calendar. The result is a tedious experience when adding new events if you always want your family member(s) to be notified.

2) Google Calendar supports fetch only, not push for updates

title: What Glitches?
body:
I never write reviews. Ever. They’re annoying and take up time I don’t have. However, I’m making an exception for this app.
	First, I keep reading review after review about how “laggy, unresponsive, and disappointing” this app is. To that I say, rubbish. I have been using Google Calendar for 10 years now, on both iOS and Android devices and have yet to come across a single issue with the app lagging. Every few months or so, I try a new calendar app just to see if I’m missing some great hidden feature out there. So far, I’ve deleted all but Google Calendar. I even have the built in iOS calendar “disabled” on all my iOS devices just so I can use Google Calendar in peace. Every time I open the calendar, it responds immediately, and open straight to the current date. 
	Second, to all those who are having trouble adding an event, I’m not sure what to say. Once again, I’ve had no issues at all with that. All my calendars sync perfectly and I’ve never had an event just disappear on me. As for the goals feature, I don’t use it. If I really want to make time for something I want to achieve, I just add it to my calendar so I know to set time aside. Maybe that’s just me being more organized than most, but I’d rather be in full control of my life goals than have to rely on an AI to schedule goals for me. 
	Finally, I understand that there are issues with apps, as there always will be due to the nature of code, but please, before you write a review, try to do a basic google search on your problem and make sure its not user error. It’s easy to blame apps and developers for issues we face, but a quick search can alleviate much frustration. 
	This review is in no way meant to belittle anyone, just simply to point out, as a long term user, that this app is fantastic. Learn its features, learn its limits, and please don’t write a poor review just because you’re frustrated. Positive criticism helps, being angry and blaming does nothing.

title: The bee’s knees!
body: I love my google calendar! She basically runs my life & holds the shattered pieces of my ADHD mind together with some semblance of dignity & adultishness. She helps me keep it all together, without forgetting important things to do in my short, mortal coil. I can color code my plans; green for the chains of duty & obligation of work, purple for holding my little social life together with the few people who tolerate my existence, blue for dreadful appointments that I must grit my teeth & bare. And I can set goals for my existentially meaningless existence just for the delusion of importance. Google can also remind me to grow up & deal with annoying details of being a citizen, like “go to the DMV, you tortoise!” I usually put these in red, to create a sense of mild threat & urgency to motivate me to act on these fiduciary commitments to the government. Thanks, google calendar, for helping me continue to exist. I do recommend this app as an act of paradoxically accepting the torment of daily living & the joy of the illusion of control before we all parish together on this giant smog-filled boulder that we are almost certainly going to blow up in war within the next generation.

title: Needs lots of functional and user interface work.
body:
This application is barely beta quality.  Editing is spotty and inconsistent.  The app cannot even get the dates and names right when importing from gmail. For example, you make a reservation at a hotel and the calendar asks you to import it; you say yes and it imports a bogus arrival date and time and bogus checkout date and time.  So you go to correct the dates and discover that you are not allowed to edit this critically important information.  You can change the color and a few minor things; but Important data such as dates and times — no, that is not allowed!? Similarly it selects the wrong name for the Hotel and you cannot correct that as well.  The application offers to show you the source email.  If you display the email it shows, shockingly, the correct hotel name and correct dates and times for check-in and out.  This function is clearly broken. 

The calendar also fails to find some of the other reservation emails.  This leads to you constructing a manual entry.  Can you attach the email to your newly constructed event?  No you cannot.  So your email is gmail and you are using the calendar app from the same company and you cannot attach the event causing email. How well thought out is that? You can’t even copy and paste the address and phone numbers; you must manually retype them.  The UI is largely inconsistent with differing ICONs for various actions with no obvious means of distinguishing actions from decorations.  So you must employ forensic discovery to find out how the actions work.

To improve the app should:  1) adopt a consistent UI paradigm so that users can distinguish between action tags and decorative tags. 2) Test using a large corpus of tests to find and fix the functional bugs.  3) Adopt an implementation mantra that directs that if a capability is allowed in one place it must be allowed in all other places where conditions are similar.  This devolves (for example) into “if you can edit a field in one form of an event then you must be able to edit that same field in all similar forms where it makes sense.” 4) Allow attachments from your own email application. 

Fix the function and improve the User interface to get this app up to professional quality.

title: Recent updates have seriously ruined this app
body:
After a few months of very laggy, unresponsive, disappointing app behavior, I finally have had enough to leave a review in the hopes that it will help someone on the app team realize just how bad things have gotten, at least for me (my wife has the same issues on her iOS devices as well, so it’s not something unique to my account). I was surprised to see how many other reviews I have found with almost exactly the same issues that I have. The fact that the other reviewers have been reporting consistently issues since at least the beginning of 2018 with no improvement is nearly inexcusable.

My primary issues in a nutshell - 1) often app opens to random dates at initial launch; 2) after initial app load, it generally takes 60-90 seconds (sometimes much longer) before the UI is responsive; 3) once everything has finally loaded (if I have not  given up and force quit it already) there is way too much UI lag and sputtering as I try to navigate through different UI views — full month, daily agenda, etc. These issues combined render the app nearly useless for me in most everyday use cases.

As an app developer myself, I can appreciate the complexity of creating a performant, well-functioning app. However, given how awesome this app used to be, and the level of satisfaction I expect from an app by Google, I’m just so frustrated and disappointed. I can’t understand why these issues have not received attention yet.

title: PLEASE FIX. THIS USED TO WORK.
body:
I used to prefer Google calendar to other ios alternatives. Now, and for the past several weeks, this app crashes and freezes so often it's nearly impossible room check appointments, navigate from month to month, let alone create new appointments. Even using safari to access GCal directly is more robust and way faster. 
These days, the only way avoid a crash, is to exit quickly, before attempting to check more than one appointment, or trying to swipe to a different date. 
I was a big fan of the interface, and I'll miss it for sure, but it's unless to keep this app, when I already have Outlook, the native ios calendar, and even GCal on a browser, all of which are faster, seldom crash, and allow all of the basic calendar functionality on my Google account. And then when I have to make an event I have to click another ‭+ sign‬ and then choose the events option— way too many clicks compared to other cal apps!!!  and then on the next Screen I have to fill out all of these fields but none of them are easy to differentiate from the other and they have too many auto populated fields that are similar… For example the word “at”.... title: Great calendar app!
body:
This is a great calendar app!  I really like all the different views that are available. I love seeing the different color codes for events, and being able to select & update the event colors on my phone in the app. Creating & finding events are easy.  Just a really great app!  
I did have one issue with the event colors, because some of them did not load the correct color when I downloaded the app. I had to manually change some of the event colors in the app to match the website / desktop version. 
There are a few things I’d like to see improve though... 
1.) The app icon should show the correct day of the week and date. 
2.) The app should add functionality to duplicate calendar entries, and then edit them, like the website / desktop version can do. 
3.) When changing / updating repeating events, add functionality to apply changes to ALL events, including past events, like the website / desktop version. 
4.) Add option to sync ALL past events, or at least last 2 or 3 years.

title: Lots of bugs to be addressed
body:

First off, it freezes ALL the time - swiping to a different week/month, adding new events, or editing current events will all freeze up the app for a significant chunk of time, sometimes upwards of a minute or more. Sometimes I’ll save an event and it’ll disappear the next time I open the app. Lately my problem has been the app quitting as soon as I open it. It’s making it extremely difficult to use this app, and frankly it’s become very unreliable to me as a student.

title: Freezes, lags, even randomly starts scrolling back to years past
body:
I want to like this app. On my laptop browser, I keep Google Calendar open in a pinned tab because I rely on and appreciate it so much. But as an app, it’s the worst thing on my phone - and I’ve kept using it because of how heavily I rely on it. But today, I’m searching the App Store for alternatives. 
A recent update said they were addressing the freezing issues some users experience. I haven’t seen improvement. This morning, I kept three people waiting so I could let them know whether I was available in two weeks - the app opened, promptly froze, and then zoomed me back to April 2017, then June 1970. I’m writing this in April 2018. The conversation moved on; ten minutes later, I was still checking the app to see if it had caught up and would allow me to scroll forward two weeks. I eventually gave up. 
Sometimes I want to edit an existing event and the window halfway opens, then lags/freezes. It takes 5-6 minutes to open, even if I close and reopen the app. 
I have no idea how to fix this. It is a wonderful, wonderful app — when it works. I can’t afford to wait for it to be fixed anymore.

title: Horrible in the last month
body:
When I first downloaded this app at the end of last year, it was fantastic. It was super easy to use, visually appealing, and everything else you could want in a working app. I don’t know what happened but it has become a nightmare to use. I can barely even input events without it immediately crashing and closing out. I then have to try to go back in to add the event again. Same thing happens again, and then I just have to give up and maybe try again later.

It also constantly freezes with no knowledge of how long it’ll sit like that. I then have to close it out and reopen it, hoping it doesn’t happen again. Which it usually does. And typically when I reopen it, I’ve lost the most recent things I’ve added into the calendar. All of this is progressively getting worse, despite the fact that Google has been sending out updates for bug fixes. Well, I don’t know what the developers are doing, but they’re not fixing any bugs. It seems as if they’re just adding more instead. PLEASE FIX IT GOOGLE. I love this calendar and the computer version. Please, please make this better. I really don’t want to have to find something else that I know really won’t be as good (that is, when this app is running at its best).

Side note: I know the problem is not my phone. I have a 256gb iPhone and I’ve used only 36gb. So, it’s not me. Also, I just want to say that leaving this review is a big deal to me. I have never once reviewed an app in my life, not even the ones that are mediocre at best and leave a lot to be desired. This is how horrible and frustrating this app has become.

title: The new updated ruined it!
body:
I have been using google calendar as my main scheduler for years. I absolutely loved it...until this year, when suddenly it started acting weird. 

First, it was glitchy and wouldn’t really save every event. 

Then, in February it began uninstalling itself several times a day, and when it WAS there, there would be the little cloud icon next to it, and if I touched the app to open, it would look like it was updating and take a minimum of ten minutes to even open. Awkward when you’re standing after a meeting scheduling the next one and you actually can’t... 

After that, it went from bad to worse. Obviously, I checked all my settings to see why it was “offloading” that app, and it actually showed that feature as turned off - it was just doing it on its own. Then, I deleted and re-downloaded the app, hoping it would make things better. It didn’t. Now, I didn’t even have the icon for the app, but when I go to the App Store, I can’t download t again because it says it’s already on my phone...which it isn’t. 

I’m so sad and frustrated! I have loved this app for years, used it multiple times daily...now, I have to start from scratch and re-imagine my own calendar with a different app and it’s kind of a nightmare.

title: Fix the performance issues!!
body:
I have lived in this app for years. I use Google for all of my productivity tools at work and personally. Google Calendar is perhaps the most important of all of these. I have never liked the native calendar apps which come with Mac OS or iOS and have exclusively used google calendar web app on desktop and google calendar iOS app on my iPhone. I interact with Google Calendar hundreds of times each day. 

For a couple of months, the iOS app has had horrendous performance issues. It lags several seconds sometimes when trying to edit an event, change its title, location, etc. I very often cannot complete a task. This is frustrating and actually causes major issues for my business. I have driven myself mad trying to fix it. I have completely reinstalled my phone twice. I have deleted and reinstalled the app countless times. I have played with and reset all settings. Etc. 

Today I saw there was a new update promising performance improvements but it is still laggy.

Guys, please fix this. I am using an iPhone 6 on iOS 11.2.6. I am generally up to date and have experienced issues since Jan 2018.

title: Infuriating to use
body:
As someone who travels a great deal work calendaring apps are and have been a mainstay in my computing and device landscape.  I began using google calendar because I like the web based version and on the road can open directions straight from calendar to google maps (my preferred navigation app) rather than Apple maps or another navigation app.  It comes in very handy when I’m the road.

That being said, as other commenters have noted creating events is a waking nightmare and exercise in frustration.  The app hangs and crashes more often than it doesn’t - seriously it’s a rare exception when I can create an event with the app that doesn’t crash it, hang so long that it’d be faster to just boot up my laptop, or look as though it saved the event when in reality it did no such thing.

It can also be pretty fickle about whether  it will load your calendars at all.

If you are in the fortunate position of never having to schedule anything when you are away from your desk and just need a way to look at your synced calendar when you are away, then you’ll be fine if the app decides to load your events at all.

But if like many of us your life is a game of scheduling Tetris and you have to schedule appointments on the fly then buyer beware.  Expect to be standing in doctors’ offices, conference halls, airports and in cabs swearing at your phone as you desperately try to make note of an appointment on your way to wherever you are going only to know in the back of your mind that it’s futile, the app won’t work,  the event won’t save and you are going to miss it and forget what you were even scheduling- only creating greater chaos in the future when you get that call “you had an appointment today at 9 am....”

title: Not quite ready for prime time
body:
I love google calendar, mostly.  I share my calendar with people I need to schedule with, and we keep synchronized.

But what really drives me crazy are monthly recurring events, of the form of “Third Wednesday of the month” or “Second Saturday of the month”.  There is no “repeat” option for these kinds of events.  I wrote a calendar app in 1977, on a timesharing system, that had this functionality in its 1.0 release.  I have been asking google for this feature for several years, and while they keep coming out with cutesy graphics and other worthless features, the fundamental functionality of monthly recurring meetings is missing.  

There are insufficient colors for all my activities, mostly because they have chosen a weird subset of colors and assigned cute names to them.  I would like to create my own colors and assign my own names to them.  Right now, “sage”=“Skype meeting”, “banana”=“medical appointment”, “Tangerine”=“writers’ group”, “grape”=“volunteer”.  I would like to say “RGB(255,255,0)”=“medical”, and have the color yellow appear as the color name “medical”.  It is annoying to have to keep this dictionary in my head; the app should help me.  I’ve been asking for this feature for years as well.  Instead, I get cutesy graphics apparently designed to appeal to 14-year-olds, not retired professionals.

So it is a tolerable app for what I need, but a far cry from a professional app designed to support real-world needs.

title: Don’t waste your time with Google Calendar App
body:
Online/Conputer version is great. App if horrible.  Don’t waste your time with the app unless you only want to visually see your appointments. Entering is worthless. 

I’ll only state two issues:

1) You can’t copy and paste and event/appointment on the app. You can only move it. So if you’re entering an appointment that you’ve had before you have to re-enter all the details from scratch.  Waste of time. You can do this directly in google via a computer, but the feature is not available on the app.

2) People that need a calendar app are typically busy people with multiple parts of their lives. It’s great the google allows you to create multiple calendars for different activities. However you can only do that online via a computer. When you create an event/appointment in the app there is no option to decide which calendar you’re creating the event for.

I could go critique the app some more, but these 2 features, which are easily done if you have a computer and are signed into google, do not carry over to the app. They are essential features. Soo essential and intuitive that when you first get the app you send lots of time looking for where the features would be because you would never think that they don’t exist on the app. You literally find yourself scratching your head as to why the features aren’t there. It basically renders the app as just a tool to view your events and nothing else.

title: Everything one might need in a calendar app
body: I love how Google Calendar automagically uploads everything to the cloud. I also love how it suggests locations based on the address one types in (of course it doesn't do this for private addresses, but it is still a handy feature.) It will set reminders by month, day, hour, or minute, and it also asks if one wants to set up recurring appointments for a number of weeks, a number of days, or annually (handy for Birthday reminders.) The app will also convert between time zones across the world—another useful feature. And all of these can easily be set whether one is using a smartphone or a tablet, and also a desktop or a laptop. All of the changes are sent to the cloud, as well. It is possible to export it into many other formats as well, such as iCal, and Microsoft Office. I ❤️ Google Calendar and will continue to use it until they pry it out of my hands. 🙂

title: I'm a convert
body: Of all the e-calendars that I've tried, I like Google calendar the best. I actually have preferred a paper date book and always end up returning to paper.  In fact I recently purchased a 2018 date book, then a 2017-18 academic year date book before deciding that I really needed to lighten my load and use a calendar on my phone since my phone is always with me.  I don't like the iPhone calendar app.   Used that for a couple of years.  I tried Outlook for a brief time.  It was better than the iPhone calendar, but I found Outlook to be cumbersome and confusing.  Google calendar is super easy to use, has some nice features, and I don't feel bombarded with too many bells and whistles that I don't need.  I'm sure the fancy stuff is there for those who need to do more complicated calendar things.  One thing though that is super easy is adding a location to your event.  I tried it for an event at a location that I'd never been to -- so simple! It practically added itself.  Another thing:  it added airline departure information that it picked up from one of my emails.  Of course, if you don't like that "how does it know what I'm doing " feeling, you can adjust what to allow in the settings.

title: Change Event from one Calendar to another
body: How about allowing us to change an event from one google calendar to another (using the iOS app).  We use one calendar for tentative events and then when the event has been confirmed we change the event to a different calendar that more people can see. They works well if you are in front of a computer but it is not possible if you are on the app.  This is hard to understand.  We are using Google calendar. We are using a Google app and main features are not available on Googles own app, but I can make this change to events on my phone, if I Sync my Google account to my iPhone and use my native iOS calendar app......Grrrr.  Why can I do more through other apps than I can with the developers own apps...not right!  I would continue to use my iOS native calendar app if it was stable. It is not. Google and Apple don't play well together as both companies are egotistical and controlling and want to have their cake and eat it too.  I don't know which is responsible it it is not stable.  Many times changes made on google don't show up on the iOS device. So I switched to using google calendar app to find out I can't edit the calendar that an event is associated with.  Anyway. This is a necessarily feature so I would HOPE it is in the process to happen soon.

title: Solid Calendar apt for busy and not so busy people
body:
I have never been a fan of the native iPhone calendar app. So I have spent many hours reviewing my options.  My biggest complaint with most apps is the weekly view is always grid based with time on he left. For those of us with few appointments, or apts. at hours spanning the day and night, this required one to constantly scroll up and down through empty, unscheduled time as you scrolled left and right through the week. 

iCalendar by Reedle solved this with their weekly block view which showed appointments in blocks right next to each other for a given day of the week, with no unscheduled time hogging up space in the screen. In an instant I can easily see days that are free and days that have scheduled blocks.

Google calendar solves this as well with their Schedule view. Showing blocks for appointments in a feed type format. One downside is that since they only list appointments it is sometimes hard to figure out what days are completely free, since it will show a appointment block for Monday and right under it the next apt let's say on Friday with no visual gap, so it's not an easy visual to see which days are completely open. Not a huge issue, it just make one have to think and not just see instantly. 

I do love the images it used to convey the appointments. It adds some flair to a usually boring visual screen of a calendar.

title: Does it's job but not intuitive
body:

I wish I didn't have to click on the "edit" button to edit it but simply tap it. That's two additional taps to change a schedule. Also, if I write, "lunch with GM at 12pm," it'd be nice if the app intuitively set the time to 12pm to 1pm. 

The design is also a bit confusing to look at. I had to scroll and focus really hard to find the "Location" to at my location. I do appreciate that it uses Google Maps to direct me to my location when I click on it. 

Lastly, it'd be great if there was a Mac app that would allow me to use it apart from the browser.

body:

This app would receive 5 stars and all the love I have in my heart if there was an option to select days of the week a certain event repeats instead of the standard "repeats every week", "repeats every day", etc. For college students who have the same classes on Monday, Wednesday, and Friday, it would be great to be able to select an option to repeat that event on certain days every week and still be able to end it on a certain day (i.e. end of the semester). As of now it's a hassle to decide, "Should I select 'repeats every day' and then delete every day it's not applicable or add a million individual events to my calendar?" Ain't nobody got time for that.

title: It's ok
body:
I love Google Calendar on my computer and I really wanted that sleek plain interface for my phone. With a family of 6 and a variety of schedules, we have about a dozen different calendars we track.

I've been using this for about a week and have only found one view that I like - the schedule view. 

For the others, I don't really need a calendar to show me days on my tiny screen with big long color blobs for the duration. Just the start time, thanks. 

Don't get me wrong - I love (and need) the colors, but I like to be able to see a week's schedule at a time easily without the fluff. If I could turn the showing of duration off, I might like it more.

Years ago I bought an app called CalenGoo, which gives me viewing options, smooth reading, and a simple interface & layout. I can see everything - still color coded - and it's not overshadowed by ribbons of color. I'll stick with that one and continue to monitor this app.

title: More Convoluted Than Necessary
body:
We should be able to set month view as the permanent view. Currently it's not, it's set up really confusing and non functional right now. I want to see the month, and add notes to the month, without it ever zooming into the day. My computer's Google Calendar allows this and it's much nicer. Please stop forcing us to micro manage our days by zooming into the day or making us write exact start and end times. I only use calendars to see what I did on a certain day, or to see future plans. I don't want to map out every minute of my day.

For example: I work on Wednesday, then I play volleyball. I would write those two things out on my calendar. I know the start and end times by heart, so writing every minute detail into the app is an annoyance. All I want to see is what I am supposed to do or what I did. It is more convenient for me to write start and end times in the titles, rather than scroll through to select day, hour, minute, am/pm, followed by making sure there was no input errors. Please appease those of us that aren't micromanagers but want to also stay organized.

title: Get it together, already, Google.
body:
This app could be so much better, if Google would actually give half a crap.  For one thing, it's absolutely shameful that the app icon STILL doesn't reflect the current date -- iCal can even do that, FFS.  The app is buggy AF, too.  Most of the time I open it, it hangs, or it takes tens of seconds before it responds to any touch commands (and with this latest update, it crashes...awesome).  Once you've created an event and saved it, you can't change which calendar it belongs to in edit mode; you can change its color, but not the calendar in which it appears.  You can't copy events from one day to another.  You can't differentiate visually between an all-day event and an event with a specific time while viewing your calendars in monthly mode.  You can't enter a location that draws information from your contacts.  You can't add it to your widgets.  You can't.  You can't.  You can't.

I want to like this app, but Google are making it impossible by not fixing obvious issues or adding common sense features.  Until they do, I'm switching to Readdle's Calendars.

title: Good start
body:
This calendar is the best of the many trials I've done over the last 5+ years. The bright colors make it easy to categorize events for our family of 6 & my office tasks. I also like that it syncs with my desktop calendar. 

Some problem features: there needs to be an easier way to "invite" others to an event. My husband & I don't need to share all tasks - but there are many that we do both need to see. It's tedious to add him to each event. There should be a quick default invite for "favorites". 

Also the way it appears on the desktop makes my head spin. I wish it showed month to month & CLEARLY highlighted the current week when viewing. When I scroll the month-view it's so hard to see the day of the month & it keeps shifting & showing part of 2 months at a time. Why not just have the 28-31 days of the month showing?? 

For this reason I avoid the desktop version to manage the schedule - though I would have used it were it easy for a 4Oish year old to see (even on my large Mac screen!)

I also wish the options for notifications could be set for my preferences. I don't want emails. 

Lastly- the ability to repeat events needs to be improved. I want to repeat on irregular days (i.e., bball April 2,7,10,18 etc.).

title: No Badge App Icons!! :/
body: I used to use Google Calendar as my only calendar and reminder app. I always had Android phones, and your reminders would remain in your status bar until you dismissed them. But when I switched over to Apple, there are no status bar reminders, you have to open the Notification Center to see everything. However, all of the apps have these convenient little red numbers on them when you haven't dealt with something in the app yet, so those are your reminders. Lamentably, Google Calendar is the ONLY app I have downloaded that doesn't have this feature. And since in the absence of status bar reminders I have come to rely so heavily on these tiny red numbers, I do not find Google Calendar preferable anymore. I could link it to Apple Calendar, but then I'd be using two apps to do the job one should be able to do. So I just started using the Apple Reminders app instead. I miss Google Calendar, but until they fix this issue, I can no longer use it :/
